gaps.sentence: He didn't ___ any interest in politics until university.
gaps.explanation: take an interest in something means to become curious or involved in it.

gaps.sentence: Students should ___ notes while they listen to the lecture.
gaps.explanation: take notes is the standard collocation for writing down information.

gaps.sentence: After six hours of talks, the two sides finally ___ an agreement.
gaps.explanation: reach an agreement/decision is the collocation; 'arrive' would need 'at', which is not in the sentence.

gaps.sentence: It took her years to ___ a living from her painting.
gaps.explanation: make a living means to earn enough money to live on.

gaps.sentence: Ordering your food online can ___ you a lot of time.
gaps.explanation: save somebody time means to make it possible for them to use less time.

gaps.sentence: I ___ hours yesterday trying to fix the printer, and it still doesn't work.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: to use time without any result
gaps.explanation: waste time means to spend time uselessly; the second clause shows there was no result.

gaps.sentence: I must ___ my homework before I can go out.
gaps.explanation: do homework is the fixed collocation; 'make homework' is a common learner error.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ interest on the money it borrows.
gaps.explanation: pay interest is the standard financial collocation.
